newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia officials sanctioned over Pacific report.
newsitem.headline: Australia officials sanctioned over Pacific report.

text.p: Four Australian Treasury officers have been disciplined after the publication of a top secret document critical of Canberra's South Pacific allies and some regional leaders which sparked an international storm.

Treasury Secretary Ted Evans told a parliamentary committee on Monday that one senior official had been barred from receiving an annual performance bonus of at least A$10,000 (US$7,400) this year and the breach had been noted in his personnel file.
Three other officials were censured over the incident, Evans told the committee hearing on government spending.

The action follows an intelligence investigation into media publication of details from the document, a secret briefing to Treasurer Peter Costello for a summit with economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum in Australia in July.
The document, marked 'Australian Eyes Only', strongly criticised some of the South Pacific economies and the personal failings of Costello's 15 guests.

Among other things, it described the drinking habits of some of the region's economic ministers and leaders, called others corrupt and branded some as incompetent. It also warned of impending economic disaster in many of the countries.
"The disclosures represented a serious breach of security," Evans said.
Details of the document were published after a Reuters journalist picked up a copy from a table in a public area at the conference venue.
Evans was giving evidence at the regular estimates hearings of parliament's upper house, the Senate.
The estimates hearings are aimed at scrutinising government spending and departments, but allow senators strong leeway to canvass a broad range of areas.
Australian diplomats in the South Pacific have spent the past weeks assuring their counterparts that the 93-page report did not reflect government policy.
South Pacific nations, such as Nauru and the Cook Islands, have said the report will damage Australia's relations with the region.
